estimate.note: GADS canonical from LOCAL reference run (drafted lane, DoWhy ATE): 0.0757, closely matching QRData's gold (0.074) — the local engine SUCCEEDED here where cloud failed twice on the identical propensity-score bug ('numpy.ndarray' object has no attribute 'iloc'). This run hit a different, non-fatal error at an earlier step ('>' not supported between 'list' and 'int' during missing-value detection) and recovered via replan, apparently sidestepping whatever code shape triggers cloud's failure. HOWEVER the reported 95% CI is degenerate ([0.0000, 0.0000]) — almost certainly a broken bootstrap/CI computation, not genuine precision — and the Synthesizer's own narrative misread this as reassuring ('narrow confidence interval indicates some uncertainty') rather than flagging it as broken. Point estimate accuracy and uncertainty-quantification correctness are being tracked as separate axes here; see notes.md. No cloud canonical value exists (see the two documented cloud failures, still below).

cloud_attempts.note: TWO independent cloud reference-run attempts (2026-08-21) both failed with the identical error ('numpy.ndarray' object has no attribute 'iloc') at the propensity-score estimation step, surviving a full model escalation ladder on the second attempt. No cloud canonical value exists for this benchmark — see notes.md. This is the inverse of the usual cloud > local assumption and is itself the finding.
